stem: The harvest festival 'Pongal' is celebrated primarily in __________.
solution: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu.

stem: The harvest festival 'Onam' is celebrated in __________.
solution: Onam is the major harvest festival of Kerala.

stem: The festival of Onam is associated with the legendary king __________.
solution: Onam celebrates the annual return of the mythical king Mahabali to Kerala.

stem: The famous snake-boat race 'Vallamkali' is held during __________.
solution: The Vallamkali (snake-boat race) is held during Onam in Kerala.

stem: The harvest festival 'Bihu' is celebrated in __________.
solution: Bihu is the harvest festival of Assam.

stem: The bonfire harvest festival 'Lohri' is celebrated in __________.
solution: Lohri is a winter harvest bonfire festival of Punjab.

stem: The harvest festival 'Baisakhi', also marking the founding of the Khalsa, is celebrated in __________.
solution: Baisakhi is a Punjabi harvest festival that also marks the founding of the Khalsa.

stem: The tribal 'Hornbill Festival' is celebrated in __________.
solution: The Hornbill Festival is the major cultural festival of Nagaland.

stem: The masked-dance 'Hemis Festival' is celebrated in __________.
solution: The Hemis Festival, with masked Cham dances, is celebrated in Ladakh.

stem: The 'Losar' festival marks the New Year of the __________ people.
solution: Losar is the Tibetan/Ladakhi New Year festival.

stem: The spring festival 'Chapchar Kut' is celebrated in __________.
solution: Chapchar Kut is a spring festival of Mizoram.

stem: The 'Ambubachi Mela' is held at the Kamakhya temple in __________.
solution: The Ambubachi Mela is held at the Kamakhya temple in Assam.

stem: The desert cultural festival 'Rann Utsav' is celebrated in __________.
solution: The Rann Utsav is held in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.

stem: The 'Kumbh Mela', the largest religious gathering, rotates among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and __________.
solution: The Kumbh Mela rotates among Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and Ujjain.

stem: The famous camel fair held in Rajasthan is the __________ Fair.
solution: The Pushkar Fair in Rajasthan is a famous camel and livestock fair.

stem: Asia's largest cattle fair, the 'Sonepur Mela', is held in __________.
solution: The Sonepur Cattle Fair (Sonepur Mela) in Bihar is one of Asia's largest.

stem: The crafts fair 'Surajkund International Crafts Mela' is held in __________.
solution: The Surajkund Crafts Mela is held in Haryana.

stem: The 'Khajuraho Dance Festival', showcasing classical dance, is held in __________.
solution: The Khajuraho Dance Festival is held against the Khajuraho temples in Madhya Pradesh.

stem: The 'Konark Dance Festival' is held near the Sun Temple in __________.
solution: The Konark Dance Festival is held near the Sun Temple in Odisha.

stem: The 'Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram) Dance Festival' is held in __________.
solution: The Mamallapuram Dance Festival is held at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu.

stem: The national academy for music, dance and drama is the __________.
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is the national academy for the performing arts.

stem: The national academy for visual (fine) arts is the __________.
solution: The Lalit Kala Akademi is the national academy of fine (visual) arts.

stem: The national academy of letters (literature) is the __________.
solution: The Sahitya Akademi is the national academy of letters (literature).

stem: The Lalit Kala Akademi and Sahitya Akademi were both established in the year __________.
solution: Both the Lalit Kala Akademi and Sahitya Akademi were established in 1954.

stem: The institution that documents and promotes India's arts research and archives, named after a former PM, is the __________.
options: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
solution: The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) documents and promotes arts research.

stem: The body responsible for the protection of ancient monuments and archaeological sites in India is the __________.
solution: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) protects monuments and archaeological sites.

stem: The Archaeological Survey of India was founded in 1861 by __________.
solution: The ASI was founded in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham.

stem: The premier institution for training in theatre, established in 1959, is the __________.
solution: The National School of Drama (NSD), New Delhi, was established in 1959.

stem: The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) is located in __________.
options: New Delhi (with branches in Mumbai and Bengaluru)
solution: The NGMA is headquartered in New Delhi with branches in Mumbai and Bengaluru.

stem: The 'Centre for Cultural Resources and Training' (CCRT) works to link __________ with education.
solution: The CCRT works to link culture with education.

stem: The seven Zonal Cultural Centres in India were set up to promote __________.
options: folk and regional arts across zones
solution: The seven Zonal Cultural Centres promote and preserve folk and regional arts.

stem: The harvest festival 'Nuakhai' is celebrated in __________.
solution: Nuakhai is a harvest festival of western Odisha.

stem: The 'Gangasagar Mela', a major pilgrimage fair, is held in __________.
solution: The Gangasagar Mela is held at Sagar Island in West Bengal.

stem: The floral carpet made during Onam is called the __________.
solution: The Pookalam is the flower-carpet arrangement made during Onam in Kerala.

stem: The 'Nagaur Fair' and 'Pushkar Fair' are livestock fairs of __________.
solution: The Nagaur and Pushkar fairs are famous livestock fairs of Rajasthan.

stem: The award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to outstanding performing artists is the __________.
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award honours outstanding performing artists.

stem: India's highest literary award, given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith, is the __________.
solution: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour.

stem: The 'Elephanta Festival' of dance and music is held near __________.
solution: The Elephanta Festival is held on Elephanta Island near Mumbai.

stem: The festival 'Makar Sankranti' is celebrated across India to mark the __________.
options: New Year of Tamil Nadu only
solution: Makar Sankranti marks the Sun's transition into Capricorn and the start of Uttarayan.

stem: The 'Modhera Dance Festival' is held at the Sun Temple in __________.
solution: The Modhera Dance Festival is held at the Sun Temple in Gujarat.

stem: The kite festival 'Uttarayan' is a major celebration in the state of __________.
solution: The international kite festival on Makar Sankranti (Uttarayan) is famous in Gujarat.

stem: The 'Thrissur Pooram', a grand temple festival with caparisoned elephants, is celebrated in __________.
solution: The Thrissur Pooram is a famous temple festival of Kerala.

stem: The tribal festival 'Sarhul', celebrating nature worship, is observed in __________.
solution: Sarhul is a nature-worship festival of the tribes of Jharkhand.

stem: The National Museum of India is located in __________.
solution: The National Museum is in New Delhi.

stem: The oldest and largest museum in India, the Indian Museum, is located in __________.
solution: The Indian Museum in Kolkata (1814) is the oldest and largest in India.

stem: The festival 'Chhath Puja', dedicated to the Sun god, is most associated with __________.
solution: Chhath Puja, worshipping the Sun, is most associated with Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh.

stem: The 'Ziro Festival of Music' is held in the state of __________.
solution: The Ziro Festival of Music is held in Arunachal Pradesh.

stem: The 'Wangala' festival of a hundred drums belongs to the __________ tribe.
solution: The Wangala (Hundred Drums) festival is celebrated by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya.

stem: The Sahitya Akademi gives its awards for excellence in __________.
solution: The Sahitya Akademi gives awards for literature in recognised Indian languages.

stem: The 'Losoong' festival, marking the harvest and New Year, is celebrated in __________.
solution: Losoong is the harvest/New Year festival of Sikkim.

stem: Cultural institutions like the Akademis were set up mainly to __________.
options: preserve, promote and support the arts
solution: The national Akademis were set up to preserve, promote and support the arts.

stem: The dance festivals held at heritage monuments help to __________.
options: promote classical arts and cultural tourism
solution: Heritage dance festivals promote the classical arts and cultural tourism.

stem: The festival 'Bonalu', dedicated to the goddess Mahakali, is celebrated in __________.
solution: Bonalu is a folk festival of Telangana honouring the goddess Mahakali.

stem: The film training institute of India, the FTII, is located in __________.
solution: The Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) is in Pune.

stem: India's fairs and festivals reflect its __________.
solution: India's fairs and festivals reflect its rich cultural, religious and regional diversity.

stem: The tea and cultural festival 'Majuli' celebrations are linked to the river island of __________.
solution: Majuli in Assam, the world's largest river island, is a centre of Vaishnava (Sattriya) culture and festivals.

stem: The 'Teej' festival, celebrating the monsoon and married women, is prominent in __________.
solution: Teej is a monsoon festival prominent in Rajasthan and North India.

stem: The three national Akademis and the NSD function under the Ministry of __________.
solution: The Akademis and NSD function under the Union Ministry of Culture.

stem: The overall purpose of preserving fairs, festivals and institutions is to sustain India's __________.
solution: Preserving these sustains India's living cultural heritage.

stem: The 'Kumbh Mela', the world's largest religious gathering, rotates among four locations including Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and:
solution: The Kumbh Mela is held by rotation at Prayagraj (Ganga-Yamuna-Saraswati), Haridwar (Ganga), Nashik (Godavari) and Ujjain (Shipra).

stem: The Kumbh Mela was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in:
solution: The Kumbh Mela was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2017, recognised as a peaceful gathering of millions of pilgrims.

stem: 'Pongal', a four-day harvest festival, is celebrated primarily in:
solution: Pongal is the major harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in January (Thai month), thanking the sun god; it corresponds to Makar Sankranti.

stem: 'Onam', the grand harvest festival marking the mythical return of King Mahabali, is celebrated in:
solution: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival celebrating the return of the benevolent King Mahabali, marked by the floral rangoli (pookalam), Vallamkali boat races and the Onasadya feast.

stem: The 'Vallamkali' (snake boat race) is a famous feature of which festival/region?
solution: Vallamkali, the snake-boat race with the long chundan vallam boats, is a highlight of Onam celebrations in Kerala, notably the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

stem: The 'Hornbill Festival', called the 'Festival of Festivals', is held annually in:
solution: The Hornbill Festival, held every December in Nagaland, showcases the culture, dances, music and cuisine of the Naga tribes; it is named after the revered hornbill bird.

stem: The 'Rann Utsav', a cultural festival held in the white salt desert, is organised in:
solution: The Rann Utsav is a vibrant cultural festival held in the Great Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, celebrating the region's crafts, music, dance and the white desert landscape.

stem: The 'Hemis Festival', celebrating Guru Padmasambhava with masked Cham dances, is held in:
solution: The Hemis Festival at Hemis Monastery in Ladakh celebrates the birth of Guru Padmasambhava with vibrant masked Cham dances performed by lamas.

stem: The 'Pushkar Fair', one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, is held in:
solution: The Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Camel Fair) in Rajasthan is a famous annual livestock fair and cultural/religious gathering around the Pushkar lake and Brahma temple.

stem: The 'Sonepur Mela', Asia's largest cattle fair, is held in:
solution: The Sonepur Mela (Harihar Kshetra Mela) in Bihar, held near the Ganga-Gandak confluence, is Asia's largest cattle fair and a major cultural gathering.

stem: The 'Rath Yatra' (chariot festival) of Lord Jagannath is world-famous and held at:
solution: The Jagannath Rath Yatra at Puri, Odisha, sees the deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra pulled on giant chariots, drawing huge crowds.

stem: The 'Bihu' festival of Assam has three forms; the spring/new-year one associated with dance and joy is:
solution: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu, in April, marks the Assamese new year and spring, celebrated with the Bihu dance and feasting; Magh (Bhogali) Bihu is the harvest festival and Kati (Kongali) Bihu a frugal one.

stem: 'Baisakhi', celebrating the harvest and the founding of the Khalsa, is a major festival of:
solution: Baisakhi (Vaisakhi), in April, is the Punjabi harvest festival and commemorates the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699; celebrated with Bhangra and Giddha.

stem: The 'Thrissur Pooram', a spectacular temple festival with caparisoned elephants and percussion, is held in:
solution: Thrissur Pooram in Kerala is a grand temple festival famous for its procession of decorated elephants, the Panchavadyam/Chenda Melam percussion and fireworks.

stem: The 'Hampi Utsav' (Vijaya Utsav) cultural festival celebrates the heritage of:
solution: The Hampi Utsav in Karnataka celebrates the rich cultural heritage of the Vijayanagara empire amid the ruins of Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stem: The 'Konark Dance Festival' is held against the backdrop of which monument?
solution: The Konark Dance Festival showcases classical dance forms against the backdrop of the Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stem: The 'Khajuraho Dance Festival' celebrates classical dance amid the temples of:
solution: The Khajuraho Dance Festival in Madhya Pradesh presents Indian classical dance forms against the backdrop of the famous Khajuraho temples, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stem: The 'Nagaur Fair' and 'Pushkar Fair' are famous as:
solution: The Nagaur Fair and Pushkar Fair are major livestock/cattle fairs of Rajasthan, combining commerce with vibrant cultural festivities.

stem: The 'Chapchar Kut', a spring festival featuring the Cheraw bamboo dance, is celebrated in:
solution: Chapchar Kut is a joyous spring festival of Mizoram celebrated after clearing the land for jhum cultivation, featuring the famous Cheraw (bamboo) dance.

stem: The 'Losar' festival, marking the new year, is celebrated by Buddhist communities of:
solution: Losar is the Tibetan Buddhist new year festival, celebrated in Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh and other Himalayan Buddhist regions with rituals, dances and feasting.

stem: 'Wangala', the 'hundred drums' festival, is the harvest festival of the ______ tribe.
solution: Wangala is the post-harvest festival of the Garo people of Meghalaya, celebrated with the '100 drums' dance in thanksgiving to the deity Saljong.

stem: The 'Ziro Festival of Music' is held in which state?
solution: The Ziro Festival of Music is an outdoor music festival held in the scenic Ziro Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, showcasing independent musicians.

stem: The 'Sammakka Saralamma Jatara' (Medaram Jatara), one of Asia's largest tribal fairs, is held in:
solution: The Medaram Jatara (Sammakka Saralamma Jatara) in Telangana is a massive biennial tribal festival honouring the goddesses Sammakka and Saralamma, drawing millions of devotees.

stem: The classical music festival 'Tyagaraja Aradhana' is held annually at Thiruvaiyaru in:
solution: The Tyagaraja Aradhana is an annual Carnatic music festival at Thiruvaiyaru, Tamil Nadu, commemorating the saint-composer Tyagaraja, where musicians sing his Pancharatna kritis.

stem: The 'Chennai Music Season' (Margazhi festival), a major cultural event, celebrates:
solution: The Chennai Music Season (December–January, the Tamil Margazhi month) is a renowned festival of Carnatic music and classical dance, with hundreds of concerts across the city.

stem: The 'Nabakalebara' ritual, involving the renewal of the wooden idols, is associated with which temple?
solution: Nabakalebara is the periodic ritual at the Jagannath Temple, Puri, in which the wooden idols of the deities are ceremonially replaced with new ones carved from sacred neem trees.

stem: 'Bonalu' and 'Bathukamma' are festivals of the goddess celebrated in:
solution: Bonalu (offering to Mahakali) and Bathukamma (the flower festival honouring goddess Gauri) are prominent cultural festivals of Telangana.

stem: The 'International Kite Festival' (Uttarayan) is famously celebrated on Makar Sankranti in:
solution: The International Kite Festival is held in Gujarat (especially Ahmedabad) on Makar Sankranti/Uttarayan, filling the skies with colourful kites.

stem: The 'Goa Carnival', a colourful street festival of parades and music, has roots in:
solution: The Goa Carnival, held before Lent, has its roots in the Portuguese Catholic tradition, featuring vibrant parades, floats, music and the figure of King Momo.

stem: The premier institution that documents and promotes India's intangible cultural heritage and festivals under UNESCO's framework is coordinated by:
solution: The Sangeet Natak Akademi serves as the nodal agency for UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage matters in India, documenting and nominating art forms and traditions.

stem: India's UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage inscriptions include Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Vedic chanting and:
options: Ramlila, Kutiyattam, Chhau and Durga Puja of Kolkata
solution: India's ICH inscriptions include Ramlila, Kutiyattam, Chhau dance, Kalbelia, Sankirtana (Manipur), Nawrouz, Yoga, Kumbh Mela and Durga Puja in Kolkata, among others.

stem: 'Durga Puja in Kolkata' was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in:
solution: Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2021, recognising its artistry, community spirit and pandal culture.

stem: 'Sankirtana', a ritual singing, drumming and dancing tradition inscribed by UNESCO, belongs to:
solution: Sankirtana of Manipur, a Vaishnavite performing-art tradition of ritual singing, drumming (pung) and dancing, was inscribed on UNESCO's ICH list in 2013.

stem: The 'Modhera Dance Festival' (Uttarardh Mahotsav) is held at the Sun Temple of:
solution: The Modhera Dance Festival is held at the Sun Temple of Modhera in Gujarat, showcasing classical dance against the historic temple backdrop.

stem: 'Teej' festivals, celebrating the monsoon and marital devotion, are especially prominent in:
solution: Teej (Hariyali, Kajari, Hartalika) festivals, celebrating the monsoon and honouring goddess Parvati, are widely observed by women in Rajasthan and North India with swings, songs and fasting.

stem: The 'Chhath Puja', a festival dedicated to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is most prominent in:
solution: Chhath Puja, dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, is a major festival of Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh, involving ritual bathing and offerings at riverbanks.

stem: 'Madai' festivals are tribal fairs celebrated by communities of:
solution: Madai is a tribal festival/fair of Chhattisgarh and central India, where communities gather to worship local deities, trade and celebrate with dance and music.

stem: 'Ambubachi Mela', a religious fair, is held at which temple in Assam?
solution: The Ambubachi Mela is a major annual fair at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, associated with the goddess's annual cycle and drawing tantric devotees.

stem: The 'Saras Mela' and various 'Surajkund' fairs primarily showcase:
solution: The Surajkund International Crafts Mela (Haryana) and Saras melas showcase India's handicrafts, handlooms, folk art, cuisine and rural culture, supporting artisans.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a festival with its state? (i) Onam – Kerala (ii) Bihu – Assam (iii) Hornbill – Nagaland
solution: All three are correct: Onam (Kerala), Bihu (Assam) and the Hornbill Festival (Nagaland) are signature festivals of their respective states.
